verdict.rationale: Bento's own docs say it trains plain-English signals on production traces that fire in real time and backfill history, and that releases are scored on live traffic as well as offline and in CI. That is direct support for continuous evaluation on production traffic. The evaluators are framed mainly as failure-mode detectors and release scoring, though, with little detail on how general-purpose evaluators are configured or what they output. missing for 10: documentation of configurable evaluator types and scoring outputs on live traffic, sampling and continuous-run controls, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can run evaluators continuously on live production traffic, not just offline datasets

citations.quote: Bento trains a detector on your own traces, fires it in real time, and backfills your history.
Every release scored against your production history — offline, in CI, and on live traffic.
The nudge ships in shadow mode, is scored against the outcome it was meant to fix
